body.translated_text: Homage to <s>Mañjuśrī</s> who abides as a youth.
Composed by the noble Lord <s>Maitreya</s>, the treatise named <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>, an instructional śāstra on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom).
First Chapter: On the Knowledge of All Aspects (<s>Sarvākārajñatā</s>).

children.translated_text: She who, through omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>), leads the <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers) who seek peace to quiescence;
She who, through path-knowledge (<s>mārgajñatā</s>), accomplishes the welfare of the world for those who work for the benefit of beings;

children.text: sarvākāramidaṃ vadanti munayo viśvaṃ yayā saṃgatās
children.translated_text: The sages who are united with her proclaim this entire [reality] in all its aspects —

children.text: tasyai śrāvakabodhisattvagaṇino buddhasya mātre namaḥ // Asa_1.1 //
children.translated_text: Homage to her, the mother of the <s>Buddha</s> who has <s>śrāvakas</s> and <s>bodhisattvas</s> as his retinue! [Asa 1.1]
Purpose of beginning the treatise: The path of the knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) which was taught here by the Teacher —
The wise desired to examine that [path] which was not grasped by others. [Asa 1.2]
And placing in memory the meaning of the <s>sūtras</s>, the tenfold practice of the <s>Dharma</s>,
They would practice [it] with ease — this is the abiding purpose of undertaking [this work]. [Asa 1.3]
Structural Arrangement of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
The <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> is expounded through eight topics:
Knowledge of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>), path-knowledge (<s>mārgajñatā</s>), omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>), then [Asa 1.4]
Complete awakening in all aspects (<s>sarvākārābhisambodha</s>), peak attainment (<s>mūrdhaprāpta</s>), the sequential [realization] (<s>anupūrvika</s>),
Awakening in a single instant (<s>ekakṣaṇābhisambodha</s>), and the <s>Dharmakāya</s> — these are the eight [topics]. [Asa 1.5]
The generation of the awakening mind (<s>cittotpāda</s>), instruction (<s>avavāda</s>), the fourfold penetrating factor (<s>nirvedhāṅga</s>),
The basis of practice (<s>ādhāra</s>) whose nature is the realm of phenomena (<s>dharmadhātu</s>), [Asa 1.6]
The object (<s>ālambana</s>), the aim (<s>samuddeśa</s>), the practices of donning armor (<s>sannāha</s>) and setting forth (<s>prasthiti</s>),
And the accumulations (<s>sambhāra</s>) together with the departure (<s>niryāṇa</s>) — [these constitute] the Sage's knowledge of all aspects. [Asa 1.7]
Obscuration (<s>dhyāmīkaraṇa</s>) and the like, and the two paths of the disciple (<s>śiṣya</s>) and the solitary realizer (<s>khaḍga</s>),
The great benefit (<s>mahānuśaṃsa</s>), the path of seeing (<s>dṛṅmārga</s>) with qualities pertaining to this and the next [world], [Asa 1.8]
Function (<s>kāritra</s>), aspiration (<s>adhimukti</s>), praise (<s>stuti</s>), eulogy (<s>stobhita</s>), and commendation (<s>śaṃsita</s>),
Dedication (<s>pariṇāma</s>), rejoicing (<s>anumodanā</s>), and two supreme mental attentions (<s>manaskāra</s>), [Asa 1.9]
Accomplishment (<s>nirhāra</s>) and ultimate purification (<s>śuddhi</s>) — this is the path of meditation (<s>bhāvanāpatha</s>);
It is taught as the path-knowledge of the <s>bodhisattvas</s> who are wise. [Asa 1.10]

children.text: prajñayā na bhave sthānaṃ kṛpayā na śame sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: Through wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), no abiding in [worldly] existence; through compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>), no abiding in quiescence;
Without skillful means (<s>upāya</s>), [nirvāṇa is] far; with skillful means, [it is] not far. [Asa 1.11]
The adverse [factor] (<s>vipakṣa</s>) and the antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>), application (<s>prayoga</s>), and its equality (<s>samatā</s>),
And the path of seeing of <s>śrāvakas</s> and others — thus omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) is taught. [Asa 1.12]
Aspects (<s>ākāra</s>) together with applications (<s>prayoga</s>), qualities (<s>guṇa</s>), faults (<s>doṣa</s>), together with characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>),
The liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) and penetration portions (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>), the trainee's (<s>śaikṣa</s>) irreversible (<s>avaivartika</s>) community — [Asa 1.13]
Equality of existence and quiescence, and unsurpassed field-purification (<s>kṣetraśuddhi</s>),
This is the complete awakening in all aspects (<s>sarvākārābhisambodha</s>), endowed with skill in means (<s>upāyakauśala</s>). [Asa 1.14]
Its sign (<s>liṅga</s>), increase (<s>vivṛddhi</s>), firmness (<s>nirūḍhi</s>), and mental stability (<s>cittasaṃsthiti</s>),
And the fourfold antidote to the fourfold conceptual elaboration (<s>vikalpa</s>), [Asa 1.15]

children.text: pratyekaṃ darśanākhye ca bhāvanākhye ca vartmani /
children.translated_text: Individually, on the path called 'seeing' (<s>darśanamārga</s>) and on the path called 'meditation' (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>),
And the uninterrupted concentration (<s>ānantaryasamādhi</s>) together with [its] deviations (<s>vipratipatti</s>) — [Asa 1.16]
The peak realization (<s>mūrdhābhisamaya</s>) is threefold; the sequential [realization] (<s>anupūrvika</s>) is tenfold;
And the awakening in a single instant (<s>ekakṣaṇābhisambodha</s>) is fourfold by characteristic. [Asa 1.17]
The natural [body] (<s>svābhāvika</s>), together with the enjoyment [body] (<s>sāmbhogika</s>), the emanation [body] (<s>nairmāṇika</s>), and likewise the other —
The <s>Dharmakāya</s> together with its activity (<s>kāritra</s>) is declared to be fourfold. [Asa 1.18]
The generation of the mind (<s>cittotpāda</s>) is the desire for perfect complete awakening (<s>samyaksambodhi</s>) for the sake of others;

children.text: samāsavyāsataḥ sā ca yathāsūtraṃ sa cocyate // Asa_1.19 //
children.translated_text: That [desire] is explained both in brief and in detail, as according to the <s>sūtras</s>, and it is [now] stated. [Asa 1.19]
By [similes of] earth, gold, moon, fire, treasure, jewel-mine, and ocean,
Diamond, mountain, medicine, friend, wish-fulfilling gem, sun, and song, [Asa 1.20]
King, storehouse, great highway, vehicle, fountain-water,
Joyful utterance, river, and cloud — it is of twenty-two kinds. [Asa 1.21]
In practice, in the truths, in the three [jewels] beginning with the <s>Buddha</s>-jewel,
Unattached, unwearied in embracing the practice, [Asa 1.22]
It is to be known in the five eyes, in the six qualities of higher knowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>),
And in the path of seeing and in [the path] called meditation — thus the instruction is tenfold. [Asa 1.23]
Those of dull and sharp faculties, those who attain through faith and through insight, those [destined for] a [certain] family,
The one-intervener, the one born in between, those who go with effort and without effort, and those going to <s>Akaniṣṭha</s>, [Asa 1.24]
Three who leap, the supreme [standing] at the peak of existence, the destroyer of form-realm attachment,
The one who attains quiescence in this very life, the body-witness, and the solitary realizer (<s>khaḍga</s>) — [these are] twenty. [Asa 1.25]
From [the perspective of] the object (<s>ālambana</s>), from the aspect (<s>ākāra</s>), from being the cause (<s>hetu</s>), from comprehension (<s>samparigraha</s>),
The noble ones who practice, each in their own way, assume the connection with the four conceptualizations (<s>vikalpa</s>). [Asa 1.26]
Compared to the <s>śrāvakas</s> together with the solitary realizers (<s>khaḍga</s>), the <s>bodhisattva</s>-protector's
[Factors of] heat (<s>ūṣman</s>) and so forth — in mild, medium, and intense [degrees] — are superior. [Asa 1.27]
The object is impermanence and so forth, based on the truths; its aspect
Is the negation of clinging and the like; the cause is for attaining the three vehicles. [Asa 1.28]
The arising and perishing of form and so forth, abiding, stability, and what is designated as inexpressible;
The state of form and the rest — through that nature, [they have] lack of inherent nature. [Asa 1.29]
The mutual inherent nature of those two, the non-establishment of their impermanence and so forth,
The emptiness of those [qualities] from having that nature, and the mutual lack of inherent nature of these two. [Asa 1.30]
The non-apprehension of phenomena, the non-examination of their signs,
And the examination by wisdom — [all] from the non-perception of everything. [Asa 1.31]
The non-self-nature of form and the rest, the nature of the absence of that,
The non-arising and non-departure of that, purity, and the signlessness of that; [Asa 1.32]
Non-reliance on those signs, non-aspiration, non-perception,
Concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), its function, prediction (<s>vyākṛti</s>), and the inexhaustibility of the mind; [Asa 1.33]
The mutual self-nature of the three, and the non-conceptualization in concentration —
Thus [is described] the penetrating portion (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>), in mild, medium, and intense [degrees]. [Asa 1.34]
The duality of conceptualization of the apprehended (<s>grāhya</s>), [distinguished] by the object and its antidote;

children.text: moharāśyādibhedena pratyekaṃ navadhā tu saḥ // Asa_1.35 //
children.translated_text: Each of these is ninefold, distinguished by the heap of delusion (<s>moha</s>) and so forth. [Asa 1.35]
The apprehender (<s>grāhaka</s>) is considered twofold, based on substance (<s>dravya</s>) and designation (<s>prajñapti</s>);
In the form of an independent self (<s>ātman</s>) and so forth, and likewise based on the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) and the like. [Asa 1.36]
Teaching [through] the non-sinking of the mind and so forth, [its] non-self-nature and so forth;
The abandonment of their adverse [factors], and the complete comprehension in every way. [Asa 1.37]
Of the sixfold realization-<s>dharma</s>, of the antidote and abandonment,

children.text: tayoḥ paryupayogasya prajñāyāḥ kṛpayā saha // Asa_1.38 //
children.translated_text: Of the employment of those two, of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) together with compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>), [Asa 1.38]
Of the uncommon nature [distinct] from disciples, of the sequential [working] for others' benefit,
And of knowledge that functions effortlessly — the foundation is called the <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage). [Asa 1.39]
Since the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of phenomena) is undivided, a division of <s>gotra</s> is not tenable;
But through the differentiation of the superimposed dharmas, that division is proclaimed. [Asa 1.40]
The object is all dharmas; these, moreover, are the wholesome (<s>kuśala</s>) and so forth,

children.text: laukikādhigamākhyāśca ye ca lokottarā matāḥ // Asa_1.41 //
children.translated_text: Those called worldly attainments and those considered supramundane (<s>lokottara</s>), [Asa 1.41]
Dharmas with and without outflows (<s>āsrava</s>), conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) and unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>),

children.text: śiṣyasādhāraṇā dharmā ye cāsādhāraṇā muneḥ // Asa_1.42 //
children.translated_text: Dharmas common to disciples and those uncommon to the Sage. [Asa 1.42]
In the three [aspects of] the mind [aspiring to] preeminence among all beings, abandonment, and realization,
The aim of the self-born ones (<s>svayambhū</s>) is to be known through three [kinds of] greatness. [Asa 1.43]

children.text: dānādau ṣaḍvidhe teṣāṃ pratyekaṃ saṃgraheṇa yā /
children.translated_text: In the sixfold [perfections] beginning with generosity (<s>dāna</s>), each one [containing] the others by way of summary —
That practice of donning armor is taught as six sets of six, as described. [Asa 1.44]
In the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions) and formless [attainments], in generosity and so forth, in the path, in loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and the like,
In the practice of non-perception of what has passed, and in the threefold purity (<s>trimaṇḍalaviśuddhi</s>), [Asa 1.45]
In the exposition, in the six <s>abhijñās</s> (higher knowledges), in the method of knowledge of all aspects,
The practice of setting forth should be known as that which mounts the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle). [Asa 1.46]
Compassion (<s>dayā</s>), the sixfold [perfections] beginning with generosity, <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) together with <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight),

children.text: yuganaddhaśca yo mārga upāye yacca kauśalam // Asa_1.47 //
children.translated_text: And the path of union (<s>yuganaddha</s>), and whatever is skill in means (<s>upāyakauśala</s>), [Asa 1.47]

children.text: jñānaṃ puṇyaṃ ca mārgaśca dhāraṇī bhūmayo daśa /
children.translated_text: Knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), merit (<s>puṇya</s>), and the path, <s>dhāraṇī</s>, the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages),
And the antidote — [this] is to be known as the sequence of the practice of accumulation. [Asa 1.48]
Intention, being beneficial in substance, equanimity toward [all] beings, [Asa 1.49]

body.translated_text: The first stage is attained through tenfold preparation:

children.translated_text: Renunciation (<s>tyāga</s>), service of [spiritual] friends, seeking the true <s>Dharma</s> as object,
Always having a mind of renunciation (<s>naiṣkramya</s>), aspiration directed toward the body of a <s>Buddha</s>, [Asa 1.50]
Teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, truthfulness — the tenth is said to be [right] speech;
And the preparation of these is to be known from the non-perception of inherent nature (<s>svabhāva</s>). [Asa 1.51]

children.text: śīlaṃ kṛtajñatā kṣāntiḥ prāmodyaṃ mahatī kṛpā /
children.translated_text: Morality (<s>śīla</s>), gratitude, patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), delight (<s>prāmodya</s>), great compassion (<s>mahākṛpā</s>),
Reverence, devoted service to the teacher (<s>guru</s>), diligence in generosity and so forth — the eighth [preparation]. [Asa 1.52]

children.text: atṛptatā śrute dānaṃ dharmasya ca nirāmiṣam /
children.translated_text: Insatiability in learning, giving of the <s>Dharma</s> without material [reward],
the purification of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field), and indefatigability in <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence). (Asa 1.53)

body.translated_text: <s>Hrī</s> (shame) and <s>apatrāpya</s> (moral dread) — this is fivefold, consisting of reflection.
Forest-dwelling, having few desires, contentment, the practice of the <s>dhūta</s> (ascetic) rules, (Asa 1.54)

children.translated_text: non-abandonment of the training, disgust toward sense-pleasures,
renunciation of all [views of] existence, and being neither withdrawn nor expectant. (Asa 1.55)

body.translated_text:
5.
<s>Sudurjayā bhūmi</s> (The Very Difficult to Conquer Stage)

children.translated_text: the ten unwholesome paths of action, (Asa 1.56)

body.translated_text: Flattery, clan-pride, [worldly] position, what leads to socializing, self-exaltation and contempt for others,

children.translated_text: pride, rigidity, perversity, wrong views, and tolerance of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) —

children.text: vivarjayan samāpnoti daśaitān pañcamī bhuvam // Asa_1.57 //
children.translated_text: by abandoning [these], one attains this fifth <s>bhūmi</s> (stage) of these ten [perfections]. (Asa 1.57)
Through the fulfillment of <s>dāna</s> (generosity), <s>śīla</s> (morality), <s>kṣamā</s> (patience), <s>vīrya</s> (vigor), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom),
one who avoids the minds of disciples, solitary realizers [who] desire [only personal liberation], and the frightened, (Asa 1.58)
who when asked is not withdrawn, and who even in total renunciation is not dejected,

children.text: kṛśo 'pi nārthināṃ kṣeptā ṣaṣṭhīṃ bhūmiṃ samaśnute // Asa_1.59 //
children.translated_text: who even when emaciated does not reject supplicants — attains the sixth <s>bhūmi</s>. (Asa 1.59)
Grasping at self, beings, life-force, person; eternalism and annihilationism;
clinging to signs and causes in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>dhātus</s> (elements), and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases); (Asa 1.60)
reliance on the three realms, attachment, withdrawn-mindedness,
and fixed adherence to the views regarding the three jewels and morality — (Asa 1.61)
dispute about <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) and its opposite — these are the twenty

children.text: kalaṅkā yasya vicchinnāḥ saptamīmetyasau bhuvam // Asa_1.62 //
children.translated_text: stains; one whose [stains] are cut off attains the seventh <s>bhūmi</s>. (Asa 1.62)
Knowledge of the three gates of liberation, purity of the three spheres,
reflection on compassion, equality of <s>dharmas</s>, knowledge of the single vehicle, (Asa 1.63)
knowledge of non-arising and patience, comprehension of <s>dharmas</s> in a single way,
the destruction of conceptual elaboration, and the abandonment of perception, views, and afflictions, (Asa 1.64)

children.text: śamathasya ca nidhyaptiḥ kauśalaṃ ca vidarśane /
children.translated_text: realization of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), and skill in <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight),

children.text: cittasya dāntatā jñānaṃ sarvatrapratighāti ca // Asa_1.65 //
children.translated_text: the taming of the mind, knowledge, and that which is unobstructed everywhere — (Asa 1.65)
non-attachment, [entry into] whichever stage one wishes, passage to other realms equally,

children.text: sarvatra svātmabhāvasya darśanaṃ ceti viṃśatiḥ // Asa_1.66 //
children.translated_text: and the seeing of one's own nature everywhere — these are the twenty [qualities]. (Asa 1.66)
Knowledge of the minds of all beings, sport with <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), auspicious
accomplishment of the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field), and examining the service of <s>Buddhas</s>, (Asa 1.67)
imperishable knowledge, purification of the <s>Jina</s>'s (Victor's) field, abiding as illusion-like,
and intentional taking of birth in existence — this eightfold activity is described. (Asa 1.68)
Infinite aspirations, knowledge of the speech of gods and others,
eloquence [flowing] like a river, and supreme entry into the womb, (Asa 1.69)
perfection of family, caste, lineage, retinue, birth,
going forth, <s>bodhi</s>-tree, and fullness of qualities — one's own attainments. (Asa 1.70)
Having crossed beyond the nine stages, one is established in the <s>Buddha</s>-stage;

children.text: yena jñānena sā jñeyā daśamī bodhisattvabhūḥ // Asa_1.71 //
children.translated_text: by which knowledge the tenth <s>bodhisattva</s>-stage should be known. (Asa 1.71)
[The Antidote-Collection] The antidote should be known as eightfold in the paths of seeing and cultivation,
for the pacification of the eight [types of] conceptual elaboration of grasped and grasper. (Asa 1.72)
In the summary, in equality, in the welfare of beings, in the abandonment of effort,

children.text: atyantāya ca niryāṇaṃ niryāṇaṃ prāptilakṣaṇam // Asa_1.73 //
children.translated_text: for the ultimate — deliverance; deliverance characterized by attainment, (Asa 1.73)
deliverance in <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience), and deliverance within the scope of the path —
this practice of deliverance should be known as eightfold in nature. (Asa 1.74)

body.translated_text: the treatise of instructions on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, [ends] the first chapter.
2. The Second Chapter: <s>Mārgajñatā</s> (Knowledge of the Paths)

children.translated_text: <s>Dhyāmīkaraṇatā</s> (dimming) by radiance, fitness for the gods,

children.text: viṣayo niyato vyāptiḥ svabhāvastasya karma ca // Asa_2.1 //
children.translated_text: a defined domain, pervasion, its nature, and its activity — (Asa 2.1)
Through the non-apprehension of the aspects of the four noble truths,
this is the path of the <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers), to be known in the system of <s>mārgajñatā</s> (path-knowledge). (Asa 2.2)
From the emptiness of form and other <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), from the non-differentiation of emptinesses,
through non-apprehension, the <s>ūṣmāṇa</s> (heat) stage; the <s>mūrdhagata</s> (summit) stage is held [to be similar]. (Asa 2.3)
The <s>kṣāntis</s> (patient acceptances), by the negation of permanence and other positions regarding those [truths],
beginning from the ten <s>bhūmis</s> (stages), through the teaching of the extensive stations — (Asa 2.4)
the <s>agradharmagata</s> (supreme worldly dharma) is declared in the path of the noble <s>śrāvakas</s>;
for what reason? Because, having awakened, the <s>Buddha</s> sees the <s>dharmas</s> as equal. (Asa 2.5)
The futility of teaching by others, self-awakening of the self-arisen ones,
and the profundity of knowledge — these are declared of the rhinoceros-like [solitary buddhas]. (Asa 2.6)

children.text: śuśrūṣā yasyā yasyārthe yatra yatra yathā yathā /
children.translated_text: Service [to the teaching]: whoever, for whatever purpose, wherever, in whatever manner,

children.text: sa so 'rthaḥ khyātyaśabdo 'pi tasya tasya tathā tathā // Asa_2.7 //
children.translated_text: that [person], that purpose — even what is inexpressible by words — thus and thus [it manifests]. (Asa 2.7)
Through the abandonment of conceptualization of the grasped object, through the non-abandonment of the grasper,
and from the basis — the summary of the rhinoceros path should be known. (Asa 2.8)
By non-contradiction with conventional designation, the form of indicating <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature of dharmas),
the <s>ūṣmagata</s> (heat) and <s>mūrdhagata</s> (summit) [stages], established through non-abandonment of form and so forth — (Asa 2.9)
through the internal emptiness and so forth, from the non-grasping of form and so forth,
the <s>kṣānti</s> (patience) [stage]; through the aspects of non-arising of form and so forth — the <s>agradharmatā</s> (supreme dharma) [stage]. (Asa 2.10)
Through the moments of patience and knowledge, fourfold for each truth,
the path of seeing in <s>mārgajñatā</s>, accompanied by benefits, is declared. (Asa 2.11)
From the absence of the relation of basis and based between <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) and awakening mutually,
alternate non-cognizance, greatness, and immeasurability, (Asa 2.12)
absence of limits of extent, the ascertainment of form and so forth,
and for one established therein — in buddhahood, non-rejection, transcendence, and so forth — (Asa 2.13)
<s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) and so forth, the attainment of emptiness, the comprehension of buddhahood,
the healing of all diseases and afflictions of complete purification, (Asa 2.14)
the pacification of grasping at <s>nirvāṇa</s>, protection from the <s>Buddhas</s> and so forth,
beginning from non-killing of beings — in the system of <s>sarvākārajñatā</s> (omniscience), (Asa 2.15)
oneself being established, the establishing, maturing of beings,
and the [dedication of] giving and so forth toward awakening — these are the moments of <s>mārgajñatā</s> (path-knowledge). (Asa 2.16)

body.translated_text: 5 - <s>Bhāvanāmārgakāritram</s> (The Activity of the Path of Meditation)

children.translated_text: 'Taming in all respects' by name — the conquest of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) in all respects,
invincibility to assault, awakening, the basis, and the [objects of] worship. (Asa 2.17)
Conviction should be known as threefold: for one's own benefit, for both one's own and others' benefit,
and for others' benefit alone — and each of these is further desired as threefold. (Asa 2.18)
Mild, medium, and intense, with divisions of mild-mild and so forth,
each again threefold — thus it is held to be twenty-sevenfold. (Asa 2.19)

body.translated_text: 7 - Praise, Commendation, and Eulogy of One with Conviction on the Path of Meditation

children.text: stutiḥ stobhaḥ praśaṃsā ca prajñāpāramitāṃ prati /
children.translated_text: Praise, commendation, and eulogy toward the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>
are desired through three sets of nine measures of conviction. (Asa 2.20)
Dedication is the distinction [and] its supreme activity;
it has the form of non-apprehension and is characterized by non-perversion. (Asa 2.21)
It is isolated, has the nature of the <s>Buddha</s>'s flood of merit, is within the range of mindfulness,
is endowed with skillful means, is signless, and is approved by the <s>Buddhas</s>. (Asa 2.22)
Not established in the three realms, the further threefold dedication:
mild, medium, and intense — having the nature of the arising of great merit. (Asa 2.23)
Through skillful means and non-apprehension, the rejoicing in roots of virtue —
rejoicing, mental attention, and contemplation are prescribed here. (Asa 2.24)
Its nature, excellence, the non-conditioning of everything,
dedication of <s>dharmas</s> through non-apprehension, and great purposefulness. (Asa 2.25)
Service of the <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>dāna</s> (generosity) and so forth, and the skill in means;
the causes of conviction here, and the causes of the deterioration of <s>dharma</s>: (Asa 2.26)
the domain of <s>Māra</s>, non-conviction in the profound <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of reality),
clinging to <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) and so forth, and association with evil friends; (Asa 2.27)
the purity of the fruit, and the purity of form and so forth — of those two
since there is no separation from their non-differentiation, purity is declared. (Asa 2.28)
Through the abandonment of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), knowable [obscurations], and the three paths of disciples, solitary ones, and <s>Jina</s>'s (Victor's) heirs,

children.text: hānād viśuddhirātyantikī tu buddhasya sarvathā // Asa_2.29 //
children.translated_text: there is purification; but for the <s>Buddha</s>, ultimate [purity] in every way. (Asa 2.29)
The path beginning with mild-mild, purification in the nine <s>bhūmis</s> (stages),
through the antidote of defilements beginning with the most intense. (Asa 2.30)
Being the antidote to the three realms, equality of the measured and the measurer,

children.text: mārgasya ceṣyate tasya codyasya parihārataḥ // Asa_2.31 //
children.translated_text: and [the nature] of that path is held, by way of answering objections. (Asa 2.31)

children.text: nāpare na pare tīre nāntarāle tayoḥ sthitā /
evaṃ kṛtvā yathokto vai jñeyaḥ sarvajñatānaye /
avikāro na karttā ca prayogo duṣkarastridhā /

body.text: caturdhāmananā tasya rūpādau samatā matā // Asa_3.10 //

children.text: pravyāhāreṇa nāsyārthaḥ pareṣu prāpyate yataḥ // Asa_3.13 //
iti seyaṃ punaḥ seyaṃ seyaṃ khalu punastridhā /
sarvajñatānāṃ traividhyāt trividhā eva te matāḥ // Asa_4.1 //
catvāraḥ pratisatyaṃ te mārge pañcadaśa smṛtāḥ // Asa_4.2 //
hetau mārge ca duḥkhe ca nirodhe ca yathākramam /
aṣṭau te sapta pañceti ṣoḍaśeti ca kīrtitāḥ // Asa_4.3 //
śiṣyāṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ buddhānāṃ ca yathākramam // Asa_4.4 //
phalaratnapradātā ca śuddhakaḥ sāvadhiśca saḥ // Asa_4.11 //
lakṣyate yena tajjñeyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ trividhaṃ ca tat /
jñānaṃ viśeṣaḥ kāritraṃ svabhāvo yaśca lakṣyate // Asa_4.13 //
ālambanaṃ ca sādhāraṃ sākalyaṃ samparigrahaḥ // Asa_4.25 //
hitaṃ sukhaṃ ca trāṇaṃ ca śaraṇaṃ layanaṃ nṛṇām /
parāyaṇaṃ ca dvīpaṃ ca pariṇāyakasaṃjñakam // Asa_4.27 //
lakṣīva lakṣyate ceti caturthaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ matam // Asa_4.31 //
ye bodhisattvā vartante so 'trāvaivartiko gaṇaḥ // Asa_4.38 //

children.translated_text: By twenty signs beginning with turning away from form and so forth,
this is the characteristic of irreversibility (<s>avaivartika</s>) of one established in the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>). // Asa 4.39 //
Turning away from form and so forth, and the destruction of moments of doubt,
when oneself is established in virtue, directing others to the same. // Asa 4.40 //
Generosity and so forth dependent on others, and non-craving even for profound meaning,
friendliness, non-association with body and so forth, and [freedom] from the fivefold obscuration. // Asa 4.41 //
Abandonment of all latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>), mindfulness and clear comprehension (<s>smṛtisamprajanya</s>), purity
of robes and so forth, and the non-arising of worms in the body. // Asa 4.42 //
Non-crookedness of mind, acceptance, freedom from jealousy and so forth of one who practices ascetic observances (<s>dhūtaguṇa</s>),
moving in accordance with the nature of things (<s>dharmatā</s>), and seeking hell for the sake of the world. // Asa 4.43 //
Not being led by others, by <s>Māra</s> who teaches another path,

children.text: māra ityeva bodhaśca caryā buddhānumoditā // Asa_4.44 //
children.translated_text: awareness that '[this is] indeed <s>Māra</s>,' and conduct approved by the <s>Buddhas</s>. // Asa 4.44 //
One established in heat (<s>ūṣman</s>), summits (<s>mūrdhan</s>), patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), and supreme dharmas (<s>agradharma</s>),
by these twenty signs, does not turn back from complete awakening (<s>sambodhi</s>). // Asa 4.45 //

children.text: kṣāntijñānakṣaṇāḥ ṣaṭ ca pañca pañca ca dṛkpathe /
children.translated_text: Six moments of patience-knowledge, and five-and-five on the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>) —
should be known as the characteristic of irreversibility of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. // Asa 4.46 //
Turning away from perception of form and so forth, firmness of mind, turning back from the two lower
vehicles, and exhaustive examination of the limbs of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and so forth. // Asa 4.47 //
Lightness of body and mind, and [celibacy being] a means for [avoiding] indulgence in desire,
perpetual <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), and purity of livelihood. // Asa 4.48 //
Regarding obstacles such as the aggregates (<s>skandha</s>) and so forth, regarding the accumulations including the faculties and so forth,

children.text: samare matsarādau ca neti yogānuyogayoḥ // Asa_4.49 //
children.translated_text: regarding battle and jealousy and so forth — 'no' in both <s>yoga</s> (practice) and pursuit. // Asa 4.49 //
Prohibition of [particular] dwelling, and non-attainment of even a particle of <s>dharma</s>,
certainty on one's own level, and abiding on the three levels (<s>bhūmi</s>). // Asa 4.50 //
Renunciation of life for the sake of the <s>Dharma</s> — these are sixteen moments
[that are] the signs of irreversibility of the wise one established on the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>). // Asa 4.51 //
The path of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>) is profound; profundity is emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) and so forth,
freedom from the extremes of superimposition (<s>samāropa</s>) and denial (<s>apavāda</s>) — that is profundity. // Asa 4.52 //
Reflection (<s>cintā</s>), weighing (<s>tulana</s>), and meditative absorption (<s>nidhyāna</s>) — repeatedly — constitute the path of meditation,

children.text: nirvedhāṅgeṣu dṛṅmārge bhāvanāmārga eva ca // Asa_4.53 //
children.translated_text: [present] in the aids to penetration (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya</s>), on the path of seeing, and on the path of meditation itself. // Asa 4.53 //
That [path] has been taught as continuous, and ninefold by way of type:
by the division of the lesser, middling, and great, again into lesser and so forth. // Asa 4.54 //
Designations such as 'incalculable' (<s>asaṃkhyeya</s>) are not appropriate in the ultimate sense;
they are outflows of compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>), accepted by the Sage (<s>Muni</s>) conventionally. // Asa 4.55 //
Decrease and increase are not applicable to a thing devoid of designation;

children.text: bhāvanākhyena kiṃ hīnaṃ vartmanā kimupadāgatam // Asa_4.56 //
children.translated_text: what is diminished by the path called 'meditation,' and what has been attained? // Asa 4.56 //
Just as <s>bodhi</s> (awakening) is, so too is the one who accomplishes the desired goal;

children.text: tathatālakṣaṇā bodhiḥ so 'pi tallakṣaṇo mataḥ // Asa_4.57 //
children.translated_text: <s>bodhi</s> is characterized by <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), and he too is considered to have that characteristic. // Asa 4.57 //

children.text: pūrveṇa bodhirno yuktā manasā paścimena vā /
children.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s> is not connected with the prior mind nor with the subsequent one;
by the analogy of the lamp, the profound nature of dharmas (<s>dharmatā</s>) is eightfold. // Asa 4.58 //

children.text: utpāde ca nirodhe ca tathatāyāṃ gabhīratā /
children.translated_text: Profundity in arising and in cessation, in <s>tathatā</s> (suchness),
in the knowable, in knowledge, in conduct, and in skillful means of non-duality (<s>advayopāyakauśala</s>). // Asa 4.59 //

body.translated_text: 9 - Equality of existence and peace (<s>bhavaśāntyoḥ samatā</s>)

children.translated_text: Due to the dream-like nature of dharmas, non-conceptualization of existence and peace;
the answers to objections such as the non-existence of <s>karma</s> are as stated. // Asa 4.60 //

body.translated_text: 10 - Unsurpassed purification of the field (<s>anuttarā kṣetraśuddhi</s>)

children.translated_text: Whatever purity of the world of sentient beings [there is], through the offering of that purity,
likewise the purity of the vessel-world (<s>bhājanaloka</s>), the <s>buddhakṣetra</s> (buddha-field). // Asa 4.61 //
The object of this practice is the transcendence of the hostile ones;
non-abiding, hitting the mark, and having an uncommon characteristic. // Asa 4.62 //
Non-attachment, non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>), and the destruction of signs (<s>nimitta</s>) and aspirations (<s>praṇidhi</s>);
its mark, and immeasurability — skillful means (<s>upāyakauśala</s>) is tenfold. // Asa 4.63 //

body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter (<s>adhikāra</s>) in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>, the treatise of instructions on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.translated_text: Even in the midst of a dream, seeing all dharmas as dream-like and so forth —

children.text: mūrdhaprāptasya yogasya liṅgaṃ dvādaśadhā matam // Asa_5.1 //
children.translated_text: the sign of the <s>yoga</s> (practice) that has reached the summit (<s>mūrdhan</s>) is considered twelvefold. // Asa 5.1 //
Taking as a comparison being born in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, worship of the <s>Buddha</s>, meritorious deeds and so forth,

children.text: upamāṃ bahudhā kṛtvā vivṛddhiḥ ṣoḍaśātmikā // Asa_5.2 //
children.translated_text: making the comparison in many ways, increase is sixteenfold. // Asa 5.2 //
The unsurpassed fulfillment of the dharmas of the three types of omniscience (<s>sarvajñatva</s>),
without abandoning the welfare of sentient beings — this is called firm establishment (<s>nirūḍhi</s>). // Asa 5.3 //
Comparable to [merit from] the four-continent, thousand-fold, two-thousand-fold, and three-thousand-fold [world systems],
by the abundance of merit through such comparisons, the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) is proclaimed. // Asa 5.4 //

children.text: pravṛttau ca nivṛttau ca pratyekaṃ tau navātmakau /
children.translated_text: In engagement (<s>pravṛtti</s>) and in cessation (<s>nivṛtti</s>), each of those two is ninefold;
the apprehended (<s>grāhya</s>) conceptualizations should be known as having the nature of erroneous objects. // Asa 5.5 //
Conceptualizations of substance (<s>dravya</s>), designation (<s>prajñapti</s>), real, and being are considered as apprehending (<s>grāhaka</s>);
by the distinction of ordinary beings (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) and noble ones (<s>ārya</s>), each of those two is ninefold. // Asa 5.6 //

children.text: grāhyau cenna tathā sto 'rthau kasya tau grāhakau matau /
children.translated_text: If the apprehended [objects] are not so and the objects do not exist as such, whose apprehenders are those two considered to be?
Thus, by the nature of apprehension, emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>) is the characteristic of those two. // Asa 5.7 //
This [conceptualization], regarding inherent nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), spiritual lineage (<s>gotra</s>), attainment, and realization,
regarding the object-support (<s>ālambana</s>) of knowledge and non-delusion, regarding antidote (<s>pratipakṣa</s>) and adversary (<s>vipakṣa</s>), // Asa 5.8 //
regarding oneself, attainment, the agent, its function, activity, and result,
the conceptualization based on the aspect of engagement is considered ninefold. // Asa 5.9 //
From falling into existence and peace, from the deficiency of realization,
from the absence of acceptance, and from the defect in what has entered the path, // Asa 5.10 //
from [knowledge] turning back upon others, from reversal in designation,
from partiality, from multiplicity, and from delusion regarding abiding and departure, // Asa 5.11 //
and from following behind — this conceptualization is ninefold;
based on the aspect of cessation, arising in the minds of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and others. // Asa 5.12 //
The first apprehender should be known [as operating] in grasping and release,
in mental activity, in the contact of the elements (<s>dhātu</s>), and of the three. // Asa 5.13 //
In abiding and in clinging, in the designation of <s>dharma</s>-substance,

children.text: saktau ca pratipakṣe ca yathecchaṃ ca gatikṣatau // Asa_5.14 //
children.translated_text: in attachment and in the antidote, in willfulness, and in the destruction of [rebirth-]destinations. // Asa 5.14 //
In going forth according to instruction, in determining path and non-path,
in cessation, in arising, and in connection and disconnection with things. // Asa 5.15 //
In the abiding and destruction of the spiritual lineage (<s>gotra</s>), in the non-existence of aspiration and cause,
and in the apprehension of an adversary — this is the other apprehending conceptualization. // Asa 5.16 //
The demonstrations of awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) for these [beings], and the gift of its cause —
the cause immediately preceding the attainment of that is characterized by abundance of merit (<s>puṇya</s>). // Asa 5.17 //
<s>Bodhi</s> (awakening) is said to be the knowledge of the extinction and non-arising of defilements (<s>mala</s>);
since there is no extinction and no arising, those are the knowable objects, in that order. // Asa 5.18 //
When the nature [of things] is unceased, through the path called 'seeing,'

children.text: vikalpajātaṃ ki kṣīṇaṃ kiṃ vānatpattimāgatam // Asa_5.19 //
children.translated_text: what conceptualization (<s>vikalpa</s>) has been destroyed? Or what has come into being? // Asa 5.19 //

children.text: sattā ca nāma dharmāṇāṃ jñeye cāvaraṇakṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The so-called existence of dharmas, and the destruction of obscurations (<s>āvaraṇa</s>) regarding the knowable —

children.text: kathyate yatparaiḥ śāsturatra vismīyate mayā // Asa_5.20 //
children.translated_text: that which is spoken of by others: 'Here I wonder at the Teacher.' // Asa 5.20 //
Nothing whatsoever is to be removed from this, nothing whatsoever is to be added;

children.text: draṣṭavyaṃ bhūtato bhūtaṃ bhūtadarśī vimucyate // Asa_5.21 //
children.translated_text: reality is to be seen as it truly is — one who sees reality is liberated. // Asa 5.21 //

children.text: ekaikasyaiva dānādau teṣāṃ yaḥ saṃgraho mithaḥ /
children.translated_text: The mutual inclusion of each of those [perfections] beginning with generosity (<s>dāna</s>) within each one —
that single-moment [realization], included in patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), is the path of seeing here. // Asa 5.22 //
Having entered that <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), then the lion's sport (<s>siṃhavijṛmbhita</s>),
[one] perceives dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) in forward and reverse order. // Asa 5.23 //
Having checked the consciousness that has obtained desire and is not concentrated,
the nine attainments including cessation, going and coming, are twofold. // Asa 5.24 //
Through the transcendence of one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, and eight [attainments],
the leaping attainment (<s>avaskanda-samāpatti</s>), without cessation, is incomparable. // Asa 5.25 //
In brief, in detail, by the <s>Buddhas</s>, with protection, in non-possession,
in the three times, in the absence of qualities, on the threefold path of the good — // Asa 5.26 //
this is one apprehended conceptualization, having the aspect of practice as its range;
the second is considered to have the activity of mind and mental factors (<s>cittacaitta</s>) as its object. // Asa 5.27 //
Non-arising of the mind, mental non-engagement at the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>),
the two mental engagements of the lesser vehicle (<s>hīnayāna</s>), and non-engagement regarding complete awakening — // Asa 5.28 //
in cultivation and non-cultivation, and the reverse of that as well —
the conceptualization on the path of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>) should be known as erroneous. // Asa 5.29 //
The first apprehender should be known as having the designation of beings (<s>sattvaprajñapti</s>) as its range,
whose nature is the investigation of the power of the emptiness of the non-reciprocity of <s>dharmas</s>. (Asa 5.30)

children.text: kṛte ca vastuno yānatritaye ca sa kīrttitaḥ /
children.translated_text: And regarding an accomplished object, in the three vehicles, it is proclaimed;

children.text: dakṣiṇāyā aśuddhau vā caryāyāśca vikopane // Asa_5.31 //
children.translated_text: in the impurity of the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (offering), or in the corruption of practice. (Asa 5.31)
Another [type], ninefold, whose domain is beings, designations, and their causes,
connected with the path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>), through the counteraction of the adverse. (Asa 5.32)
Regarding the three omnisciences (<s>sarvajñatā</s>), each in its respective threefold envelopment,
in the conjunction and disjunction of the path of peace, suchness (<s>tathatā</s>), and so forth; (Asa 5.33)
and in inequality with respect to suffering and the like, and in the nature of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),

children.text: dvayābhāve ca saṃmohe vikalpaḥ paścimo mataḥ // Asa_5.34 //
children.translated_text: and in the absence of duality, and in delusion — the last [type of] conceptual construction is taught. (Asa 5.34)
Upon the cessation of these [conceptual constructions] that had been, like the gasps of one long suffocated,
the excellences of qualities — means for the happiness of the entire world in all its aspects — [arise]. (Asa 5.35)
All [excellences], through complete pursuit, [enter into] that which bears the fruit of complete satisfaction;
they serve that great being (<s>mahāsattva</s>) as rivers [serve] the great ocean. (Asa 5.36)
Having established beings of the three-thousand [world-system] in the accomplishment of the disciple's, solitary realizer's (<s>khaḍga</s>), and higher attainments,

children.text: bodhisattvasya ca nyāme pratiṣṭhāpya śubhopamāḥ // Asa_5.37 //
children.translated_text: and in the discipline of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, [these are] likened to the auspicious. (Asa 5.37)
By the abundance of merit, immediately [leading to] the attainment of <s>Buddhahood</s>,

children.text: ānantaryasamādhiḥ sa sarvākārajñatā ca tat // Asa_5.38 //
children.translated_text: that is the <s>Ānantaryasamādhi</s> (Immediate Concentration), and that [constitutes] the omniscience of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>). (Asa 5.38)
Its object (<s>ālambana</s>) is non-existence; and its sovereign (<s>adhipati</s>) is considered to be mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>);
its aspect (<s>ākāra</s>) is peace; and here, for those who propound assertions and non-assertions. (Asa 5.39)
Regarding the occurrence of the object (<s>ālambana</s>), and the ascertainment of its own nature,
regarding the knowledge of the omniscience of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>), regarding the ultimate (<s>paramārtha</s>) together with the conventional (<s>saṃvṛti</s>); (Asa 5.40)

children.text: prayoge triṣu ratneṣu sopāye samaye muneḥ /
children.translated_text: in application, in the three jewels (<s>ratna</s>), in [the path] with means (<s>sopāya</s>), in the commitment (<s>samaya</s>) of the sage,
in error (<s>viparyāsa</s>), in the correct path, and regarding the counterpart and the adverse — (Asa 5.41)
in the definition and in the cultivation — the disagreements [of the disputants] are recognized;

children.text: sarvākārajñatādhārā ṣoḍhā daśa ca vādinām // Asa_5.42 //
children.translated_text: based on the omniscience of all aspects, they are sixteenfold — ten, and [further distinctions] of the disputants. (Asa 5.42)

body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the fifth chapter in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>, the treatise of instruction on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom).

children.text: dānena prajñayā yāvad buddhādau smṛtibhiśca sā /
children.translated_text: Through generosity (<s>dāna</s>), through wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), as far as the <s>Buddha</s> and others, and through mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>),
by the nature of the non-existence of <s>dharmas</s> — thus the sequential practice is taught. (Asa 6.1)

body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the sixth chapter in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>, the treatise of instruction on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

children.translated_text: Because all uncontaminated [<s>dharmas</s>] are comprised even by a single one,
this instantaneous awakening of the sage should be known through generosity (<s>dāna</s>) and the rest. (Asa 7.1)
Just as even a single plank of a water-wheel, set in motion by a person,

children.text: sakṛt sarvaṃ cālayati jñānamekakṣaṇe tathā // Asa_7.2 //
children.translated_text: sets the whole [wheel] in motion at once — so too is knowledge in a single instant. (Asa 7.2)
When the condition of the maturation of <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality) has become entirely pure,
the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom) has arisen — then is knowledge in a single instant. (Asa 7.3)
Abiding in <s>dharmas</s> that are like a dream, through the practice of generosity and the rest,
one finds the non-characterization of <s>dharmas</s> in a single instant. (Asa 7.4)
One does not see the dream and the one who sees the dream through the conjunction of duality;
one sees the non-dual reality of <s>dharmas</s> in a single instant. (Asa 7.5)

body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the seventh chapter in the <s>Abhisamayālaṅkāra</s>, the treatise of instruction on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.
The eighth chapter: <s>Dharmakāyādhikāra</s> (The <s>Dharmakāya</s>, Body of Dharma)

children.text: sarvākārāṃ viśuddhiṃ ye dharmāḥ prāptā nirāsravāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those uncontaminated <s>dharmas</s> that have attained the complete purity of all aspects —
the <s>Svabhāvakāya</s> (Essential Body) of the sage is characterized by their [very] nature. (Asa 8.1)
The factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣa</s>), the immeasurables (<s>apramāṇa</s>), the liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>) in succession,
the ninefold attainment (<s>samāpatti</s>), the totality (<s>kṛtsna</s>) of tenfold nature; (Asa 8.2)
the bases of mastery (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>), eightfold in their divisions,
<s>araṇā</s> (non-conflict), the cognition of aspiration (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>), the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), the analytical knowledges (<s>pratisaṃvid</s>); (Asa 8.3)
all the aspects, then the four purifications (<s>śuddhi</s>), the ten masteries (<s>vaśitā</s>),
the ten powers (<s>bala</s>), the four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), non-guarding (<s>arakṣaṇa</s>); (Asa 8.4)
the threefold establishment of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), the threefold nature of non-delusion (<s>asaṃmoṣadharmatā</s>),

children.text: vāsanāyāḥ samudghāto mahatī karuṇā jane // Asa_8.5 //
children.translated_text: the eradication of latent tendencies (<s>vāsanā</s>), and great compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) toward beings; (Asa 8.5)
the eighteen qualities exclusive (<s>āveṇika</s>) to the sage alone, which have been proclaimed,
and the omniscience of all aspects (<s>sarvākārajñatā</s>) — this is called the <s>Dharmakāya</s> (Body of Dharma). (Asa 8.6)
Of the <s>śrāvaka</s> (hearer), the <s>araṇā</s> (non-conflict) vision [removes only] human afflictions;
for the complete severing of the stream of their afflictions — [there is] the <s>araṇā</s> of the <s>Jina</s> (Victorious One) in villages and such. (Asa 8.7)
Effortless, unattached, unobstructed, always abiding,
answering all questions — this is recognized as the <s>Buddha's</s> cognition of aspiration (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>). (Asa 8.8)

children.text: paripākaṃ gate hetau yasya yasya yadā yadā /
children.translated_text: When the cause has come to maturation, for whomever and whenever

children.text: hitaṃ bhavati karttavyaṃ prathate tasya tasya saḥ // Asa_8.9 //
children.translated_text: it becomes beneficial to act — to that one, at that time, he manifests. (Asa 8.9)

children.text: varṣatyapi hi parjanye naiva bījaṃ prarohati /
children.translated_text: For even when the rain-cloud (<s>parjanya</s>) rains, a seed does not sprout [without conditions];
even with the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>, one who is not [spiritually] fit does not attain the good. (Asa 8.10)
Thus, because of the vastness of [his] activity, the <s>Buddha</s> is called all-pervading;

children.text: akṣayatvācca tasyaiva nitya ityapi kathyate // Asa_8.11 //
children.translated_text: and because of the imperishability of that very [activity], he is also called eternal. (Asa 8.11)
This body of the sage, consisting of the thirty-two marks (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) and eighty minor marks (<s>vyañjana</s>),
is considered the <s>Sāṃbhogika</s> (Enjoyment) Body, from the enjoyment of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. (Asa 8.12)
Wheel-marked hands, feet with the tortoise-gait, web-covered fingers of hands and feet,

children.text: karau sapādau taruṇau mṛdū ca samutsadai saptabhirāśrayo 'sya // Asa_8.13 //
children.translated_text: hands and feet that are youthful and soft, and [a body] supported by seven prominences; (Asa 8.13)
long fingers, a body with extended heels, tall, straight, with conch-shaped ankles, and upward-growing body hair,
antelope-like calves, with broad thighs and arms, and the male organ concealed in a sheath; (Asa 8.14)
of golden color, with fine skin, each hair growing singly and turning to the right,

children.text: ūrṇāṅkitāsyo haripūrvakāyaḥ skandhau vṛtāvasya citāntarāṃsaḥ // Asa_8.15 //
children.translated_text: face marked with the <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between eyebrows), lion-like upper body, rounded shoulders with full space between them; (Asa 8.15)
the inferior taste is unknown [to him], the supreme taste is his, with a body proportioned like a <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) tree,

children.text: uṣṇīṣamūrdhā pṛthucārujivho brahmasvaraḥ siṃhahanuḥ suśuklāḥ // Asa_8.16 //
children.translated_text: an <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance) on the head, broad and beautiful tongue, voice of <s>Brahmā</s>, lion-like jaw, pure white [teeth]; (Asa 8.16)
teeth equal in size, without gaps, four sets of ten in number, not deficient,

children.text: nīlekṣaṇo govṛṣapakṣmanetro dvātriṃśadetāni hi lakṣaṇāni // Asa_8.17 //
children.translated_text: blue eyes, eyelashes like those of a bull — these are the thirty-two marks. (Asa 8.17)
Whatever cause is the accomplisher of whatever mark,
by fulfilling that [cause], this is the characteristic of [the mark's] production. (Asa 8.18)
Following after elders, firmness regarding the discipline (<s>saṃvara</s>),

children.text: saṃgrahāsevanaṃ dānaṃ praṇītasya ca vastunaḥ // Asa_8.19 //
children.translated_text: gathering [beings], practice, and the giving of excellent things; (Asa 8.19)
the undertaking of liberating those condemned to death, and the increase of what is wholesome —
such, according to the <s>sūtras</s>, are the causes that accomplish the marks. (Asa 8.20)

children.text: tāmrāḥ snigdhāśca tuṅgāśca nakhā aṅgulayo muneḥ /
children.translated_text: The sage's nails are copper-colored, smooth, and raised; the fingers
are round, tapering in order, with hidden veins free from knots; (Asa 8.21)
hidden ankles, even feet; the gait of a lion, elephant, bull, and king of geese;
[his] stride is to the right, [his] walk is graceful, [his body is] straight and round. (Asa 8.22)
Fists tapering in order, [body] clean, soft, and with a pure body,
distinguished by the preceding minor marks, with a beautifully broad and rounded body; (Asa 8.23)
even gait, purity and delicacy of the eyes,
un-depressed and prominent body, well-knit and firm body; (Asa 8.24)
well-proportioned limbs, sight purified of the destruction of darkness,
round, smooth, unwounded, not-thin belly, and profundity; (Asa 8.25)
a navel turning to the right, beautiful to behold from all sides,
proper conduct, purity, body free from moles and marks; (Asa 8.26)
hands [soft as] cotton, soft, smooth, profound, extended lines,
speech not too long, lips comparable to <s>bimba</s> fruit and its reflection; (Asa 8.27)

children.text: mṛdvī tanvī ca raktā ca jivhā jīmūtaghoṣatā /
children.translated_text: tongue soft, slender, and red, voice like thunder,

children.text: cārūmañjusvaro daṃṣṭrā vṛttāstīkṣṇāḥ sitāḥ samāḥ // Asa_8.28 //
children.translated_text: beautiful and sweet voice, fangs round, sharp, white, and even; (Asa 8.28)
gradual in progression, raised, nose supremely pure,
wide eyes with thick lashes, marked like lotus petals; (Asa 8.29)
elongated, smooth, well-oiled, even brows; arms
full and extended; ears even, free from defect; (Asa 8.30)
an unfading forehead, full and broad head,
hair thick, glossy, smooth, with undisturbed form; (Asa 8.31)
hair not coarse, stealing away the fragrance of men,

children.text: śrīvatsaḥ svastikaṃ ceti buddhānuvyañjanaṃ matam // Asa_8.32 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> and the <s>Svastika</s> — these are considered the minor marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>) of the <s>Buddha</s>. (Asa 8.32)

children.text: karoti yena citrāṇi hitāni jagataḥ samam /
children.translated_text: That by which he performs various activities beneficial to the world equally,

children.text: ābhavāt so 'nupacchinnaḥ kāyo nairmāṇiko muneḥ // Asa_8.33 //
children.translated_text: uninterrupted until the end of existence — that is the <s>Nairmāṇikakāya</s> (Emanation Body) of the sage. (Asa 8.33)
Likewise, the activities of the <s>Buddha</s>, and his actions too, are uninterrupted throughout <s>saṃsāra</s> — thus it is held.

children.text: gatīnāṃ śamanaṃ karma saṃgrahe ca caturvidhe // Asa_8.34 //
children.translated_text: The pacification of [rebirth in the lower] destinies (<s>gati</s>), activity in the fourfold means of attraction (<s>saṃgraha</s>), // Asa_8.34 //
Establishing [beings] in [the understanding of] defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) and purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>),
In the true nature of the aims of beings, and in the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), // Asa_8.35 //
In the path of the <s>Buddha</s>, in <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) by its very nature, in the cessation of duality,

children.text: saṃkete 'nupalambhe ca paripāke ca dehinām // Asa_8.36 //
children.translated_text: In conventional designation (<s>saṃketa</s>), in non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>), and in the maturation (<s>paripāka</s>) of embodied beings, // Asa_8.36 //
In the path of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, in the removal of attachment (<s>abhiniveśa</s>),
In the attainment of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), in the purification of the <s>Buddha</s>-field (<s>jinakṣetra</s>), regarding certainty (<s>niyati</s>), // Asa_8.37 //
In the immeasurable welfare of beings, in the qualities beginning with serving the <s>Buddhas</s>,
In the limbs of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), in the non-destruction of actions, in the vision of truth (<s>satyadarśana</s>), // Asa_8.38 //
In the abandonment of erroneous views (<s>viparyāsa</s>), and in establishing their substancelessness,
In purification together with its accumulations (<s>sambhāra</s>), regarding the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>) and the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>), // Asa_8.39 //
In the non-complete-knowledge of distinction, and establishing in <s>nirvāṇa</s> —
This activity of the <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth-body) is regarded as twenty-seven-fold. // Asa_8.40 //

body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the eighth chapter in the <s>Abhisamayālaṃkāra</s>, the instructional treatise on the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> (Perfection of Wisdom). /
